title: Election: God's Choosing
lead: The Bible says God chose Abraham's family, and Israel among the nations, not for their merit but out of love (Deuteronomy 7:6–8). Paul uses Jacob and Esau to argue that God's choosing does not depend on works (Romans 9:10–13). Christians differ on whether this speaks of individuals chosen for salvation or of peoples chosen for a role in history.

sections.b: Augustine and later Calvin read Romans 9 as God's choice of individuals for salvation, made before birth. Arminian and many Catholic and Orthodox interpreters hold that God's choice is based on his foreknowledge or concerns peoples and their roles (Israel and Edom, as in Malachi 1:2–4). Jewish tradition speaks of Israel's chosenness as a calling to God's covenant and commandments (Exodus 19:5–6; Amos 3:2), and many Jewish thinkers stress that it brings responsibility, not privilege. All agree that in Genesis God's choice repeatedly falls on the unexpected, younger or weaker one.
